newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes on highs, seen well supported.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes on highs, seen well supported.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on its highs in quiet Monday trade and was seen continuing its upward grind.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.7091/98 and 67.71 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7083/90 and 67.65 in the morning.
A Wellington dealer said he saw support moving up to the 0.7040/50 area from around 0.7025 last week, and a likely range of 0.7050-7150 for the remainder of the week.

"One would have to expect further gains would be in store for the Kiwi," an Auckland trader said. "It's the same scenario: demand from offshore, locals are short, it's still a good place to put your money at the end of the day."

He said volatility in dollar/yen and dollar/mark had been a feature of the session, stemming from concern about President Boris Yeltsin's health and rumours of a coup in Russia. The Russian defence ministry said there was no truth in the rumours.
The dealer expected the New Zealand dollar to break above 71 U.S. cents overnight, though he said it may initially struggle just above that level.

"Certainly you've got to see it higher, back up to the highs of (just under) 0.7150 some time in the not too distant future. It's still at the end of the day a well-bid and well sought-after unit," he said.
